constraints.message: IrreversibleActionAttestation: the actor that proposes an irreversible action MUST NOT be the actor that executes it (proposer_is_not_executor). A separation_of_duties.waiver_reference does not relax this rule inside validate().
constraints.evaluation_note: Library-evaluated by the registered cross-field validator validateIrreversibleActionAttestation. Exact string equality; the library does not normalise actor identifiers (non-constraint IAA-N3). A waiver is informational (IAA-N5): a consumer that honours waivers decides what to do with IAA-1 errors outside validate().

constraints.message: IrreversibleActionAttestation: proposal and execution MUST be made under different signer keys. A separation_of_duties.waiver_reference does not relax this rule inside validate().
constraints.evaluation_note: Library-evaluated by the registered cross-field validator. signer_key_id is pinned to 64 lowercase hex characters so exact string inequality is inequality of key identifiers (a mixed-case alphabet would let one key appear as two identifiers). Proving the two keys belong to different principals is consumer keyring state (non-constraint IAA-N4).

constraints.message: IrreversibleActionAttestation: execution.executed_at MUST NOT be before proposal.proposed_at. Equal instants are admitted.
constraints.evaluation_note: Library-evaluated by the registered cross-field validator, which compares the two ISO 8601 UTC instants exactly at nanosecond precision and handles mixed fractional precision (00:00:00Z equals 00:00:00.000Z). The DSL restatement uses the is_after builtin, which compares at millisecond precision; the two agree whenever the instants differ by at least one millisecond, and the cross-field validator is authoritative below that. No maximum gap between proposal and execution is imposed (non-constraint IAA-N6).

constraints.message: IrreversibleActionAttestation: target.schema_id MUST be a non-empty PascalCase identifier of at most 128 characters matching ^[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9]*$. The PascalCase predicate ^[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9]*$ is enforced only by the structural tier (the schema pattern); the DSL row restates only the length bounds (1..128) for cross-runner parity, so a DSL-only evaluation of IAA-4 is NOT equivalent to the structural check.
constraints.evaluation_note: Structural-tier rule. The PascalCase predicate ^[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9]*$ is enforced only by the structural tier (the schema pattern); the DSL row restates only the length bounds (1..128) for cross-runner parity, so a DSL-only evaluation of IAA-4 is NOT equivalent to the structural check. The constraint DSL has no regular-expression builtin and none is added for this rule. Cross-language runners reject non-PascalCase values from the generated JSON Schema pattern, not from this expression. The constraint-file format has no structural-only marker, so this note records the layer.

constraints.expression: consumer verifies every present signature under its keyring: proposal.signature over the RFC 8785 JCS bytes of the attestation with execution and proposal.signature removed; execution.signature over the JCS bytes of the attestation with execution.signature removed
constraints.message: IrreversibleActionAttestation: present signatures MUST verify under the consumer keyring. The library does not verify signatures; validate() fails closed with CRYPTO_DEFERRED unless the caller passes acceptDeferred.
constraints.evaluation_note: Runtime-deferred with reason crypto_deferred. The schema is x-crypto-bearing, so validate() returns CRYPTO_DEFERRED unless the consumer opts in to shape-only validation with acceptDeferred: true, in which case the CRYPTO_DEFERRED obligation is surfaced in the unverified-obligations manifest. The signing input binds the whole envelope (target and action_kind included), not only the signer's own sub-object, so a proposal signature cannot be replayed onto another target. Hounfour ships no ed25519 verifier (ADR-010 RULE-2). Key-to-actor binding is consumer keyring state (non-constraint IAA-N7).
